headline: February was the month coding agents went from demo to default: Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.3 Codex launched almost simultaneously, OpenClaw popularized personal agent teams, and software stocks sold off on the prospect. Underneath it ran a fight over who controls frontier AI, from the Anthropic-Pentagon standoff to the capital, chips and power needed to keep scaling.

themes.title: Coding agents become the inflection point
themes.body: NLW argues the near-simultaneous Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.3 Codex launches capped a run of recognitions that agents now do real work, shifting debate from an AI bubble to underbuilt compute, and reads SemiAnalysis's 'Claude Code is the Inflection Point'. SemiAnalysis's Doug O'Laughlin describes his own Claude Code 'psychosis' and tracks its share of GitHub commits. Blitzy pitches enterprise-scale autonomous code generation, Jeff Dean says coding agents change software work, and Spotify engineers reportedly no longer hand-code. Mitchell Hashimoto says AI pull requests push open source toward default deny.

themes.title: OpenClaw and personal agent teams
themes.body: OpenClaw was the month's breakout open-source agent. Lex Fridman's guest Peter Steinberger recounts its one-hour origin, the rename saga, security concerns and acquisition talks with Meta and OpenAI; he then joined OpenAI while OpenClaw moved to a foundation. NLW built a 10-agent OpenClaw team on a Mac Mini and argues products like Claude Code Remote Control, Perplexity Computer and Notion Custom Agents copy its primitives. Malware in its skills library and the Moltbook agent network showed the security risks.

themes.title: The SaaSpocalypse and AI capital
themes.body: A software stock sell-off, triggered partly by a Claude Cowork legal plugin, spread to Monday.com, wealth managers and cybersecurity names. Sarah Guo and Elad Gil argue the panic projects small-startup vibe-coding onto large enterprises and point to bundling as a defense. a16z's Martin Casado and Sarah Wang say frontier labs' capital flywheel may let them outspend apps built on top. Meanwhile Anthropic raised $30B at $380B and OpenAI accelerated IPO plans.

themes.title: Work, jobs and productivity
themes.body: Block cut over 4,000 staff, about 40%, with Jack Dorsey citing intelligence tools, though skeptics blamed COVID overhiring. Erik Brynjolfsson reads revised US labor data as an AI productivity boom, while a Berkeley Haas study finds AI intensifies work. NLW's survey of 583 listeners puts time savings third behind output and new capabilities. Matt Shumer's viral essay says knowledge work is next. Deloitte's Deborah Golden stresses the cognitive load of working with agents.

themes.title: Who controls frontier AI
themes.body: The Anthropic-Pentagon dispute escalated all month and ended with President Trump ordering agencies to stop using Anthropic and Hegseth designating it a supply chain risk, while OpenAI signed a classified deal with the Department of War. NLW surveys debates on corporate red lines and democratic control. Dario Amodei discusses state laws and export controls, Sam Hammond covers US policy and Gulf compute deals, and Jeremie Harris addresses US-China dynamics and export controls.

themes.title: Compute, power and the buildout
themes.body: Google and Amazon earnings pushed big-tech 2026 AI capex to about $650 billion. Elon Musk tells Dwarkesh that power limits will make space the cheapest place for AI compute within about 36 months, as SpaceX acquired xAI at a combined $1.25 trillion. Magnetar's Neil Tiwari explains SPV debt backed by contracted cash flows and bottlenecks like steel and electricians. Doug O'Laughlin flags a DRAM/HBM shortage, and Dario Amodei explains how Anthropic sizes compute purchases.

themes.title: Benchmarks break down
themes.body: OpenAI's Mia Glaese and Olivia Watkins explain why SWE-Bench Verified is retired as saturated and contaminated, recommending SWE-Bench Pro; Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discuss the same move and Anthropic's distillation allegations. METR's results put Opus 4.6 at about 14.5 hours, with noise caveats, and Joel Becker covers harness overfitting. Sean McGregor works on meta-evaluation of benchmarks, and NLW says benchmark leadership now rotates weekly, so cost and specific capabilities matter more.

themes.title: AI for science and health
themes.body: Several guests described AI aimed at discovery. OpenAI's Karan Singhal covers ChatGPT Health, HealthBench and the Penda Health copilot trial. Harmonic's Lean-based Aristotle reached IMO gold level. Boltz is open-sourcing structural biology models beyond AlphaFold, and CuspAI searches material space with humans in the loop. Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan pair a frontier biology lab with an AI lab at the Biohub, and James Zou and Abhi Mahajan discuss multi-agent science and cancer foundation models.

themes.title: Security, safety and interpretability
themes.body: Alexis Carlier of Asymmetric Security argues AI can make digital forensics continuous and that defensive capabilities should be accelerated. Goodfire AI, raising a $150M Series B, shows production interpretability such as Rakuten PII detection and live steering on Kimi K2. Helen Toner presents CSET's report on automated AI R&D, Shoshannah Tekofsky reports deception findings from AI Village, and Sean McGregor catalogues AI incidents. Claude Code Security prompted a cybersecurity stock selloff.

themes.title: Public backlash against AI
themes.body: Time's 'The People vs. AI' cover prompted NLW to sort anti-AI sentiment into groups, from safety advocates and bubble skeptics to data center opponents and job displacement concerns; he argues many concerns are good-faith and solvable. AI Super Bowl ads from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and others ran against polling that shows American skepticism. Hollywood pushed back on ByteDance's Seedance 2.0, and data center politics drew a White House community pact.

implications: Coding agents now do sustained, multi-hour work. Treat agent-assisted development as the default engineering workflow and invest in review, testing and repository context so agent output can be trusted at scale.

Personal agent frameworks like OpenClaw spread faster than governance. Inventory where employees run agents, which credentials and skills they load, and set sandboxing and approval rules before an incident forces them.

Public benchmarks are saturating and contaminated, and leadership rotates weekly. Build internal evaluations on your own tasks, weigh cost and specific capabilities, and keep model choice swappable behind an abstraction layer.

Vendor access can change for political reasons, as the Anthropic-Pentagon dispute showed. Keep a multi-model strategy with tested fallbacks and contract terms that address usage restrictions and sudden policy shifts.

Evidence on productivity is mixed: output and new capabilities rise, but work can intensify. Measure outcomes rather than time saved, and plan for the cognitive load and role changes that come with supervising agents.

episodes.title: Are 40% Staff Cuts the New AI Normal?
episodes.summary: The main episode covers Block's layoff of over 4,000 employees, about 40% of staff, with Jack Dorsey citing intelligence tools, plus skepticism that it was COVID overhiring and the stock's 25% jump. Headlines cover Google's Nano Banana 2, Claude signup growth, IBM's drop over a COBOL blog post, Meta scaling back custom chips, and Microsoft Copilot Tasks.

episodes.title: Who Controls AI?
episodes.summary: NLW recounts the Anthropic-Pentagon standoff culminating in President Trump ordering federal agencies to stop using Anthropic and Hegseth designating it a supply chain risk, while OpenAI reached a classified deployment deal with the Department of War. He surveys reactions on corporate red lines, democratic control of the military, retaliation, and public opinion.

episodes.title: METR’s Joel Becker on exponential Time Horizon Evals, Threat Models, and the Limits of AI Productivity
episodes.summary: Joel Becker of METR explains the time horizon evaluation, how tasks are selected, Opus 4.5's jump, and the difficulty of rerunning METR's developer productivity RCT. The conversation also covers capability explosion threat models, compute-driven slowdown research, harness overfitting, prediction markets and Becker's Manifold trading story.

episodes.title: The OpenClaw-ification of AI
episodes.summary: NLW argues products like Claude Code Remote Control, Cowork Scheduled Tasks, Perplexity Computer and Notion Custom Agents reflect new agentic primitives popularized by OpenClaw. Headlines cover the Pentagon's ultimatum to Anthropic, reports that Stargate has stalled, and NVIDIA's record earnings.

episodes.title: [LIVE] Anthropic Distillation & How Models Cheat (SWE-Bench Dead) | Nathan Lambert & Sebastian Raschka
episodes.summary: A SAIL Live session with Nathan Lambert, Sebastian Raschka and swyx discussing Anthropic's blog post alleging large-scale distillation by Chinese labs, how distillation works and is detected, and whether labs will keep models out of APIs. The second half covers OpenAI deprecating SWE-bench Verified over unsolvable tasks and contamination, and the move to SWE-bench Pro.

episodes.title: How Capital is Powering the AI Infrastructure Buildout with Magnetar Capital Managing Director Neil Tiwari
episodes.summary: Sarah Guo interviews Neil Tiwari of Magnetar Capital about financing the AI compute buildout, from Magnetar's early CoreWeave investment to SPV debt structures backed by contracted cash flows. They cover circular-financing critiques, the shift to distributed inference, power and supply bottlenecks such as steel and electricians, sovereign compute, physical AI, and the market rotation out of SaaS.

episodes.title: Universal Medical Intelligence: OpenAI's Plan to Elevate Human Health, with Karan Singhal
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews Karan Singhal, head of Health AI at OpenAI, about ChatGPT Health, ChatGPT for Healthcare, the HealthBench evaluation and the Penda Health clinical copilot trial. They also discuss Nathan's use of frontier models during his son's cancer treatment, privacy, calibration, chain-of-thought monitorability, scalable oversight and the future of medical AI.

episodes.title: 🔬 Searching the Space of All Possible Materials — Prof. Max Welling, CuspAI
episodes.summary: Prof. Max Welling discusses his path from quantum gravity to machine learning, CuspAI's AI platform for searching material space, and why humans stay in the loop. He also explains equivariance and his upcoming book linking generative AI and stochastic thermodynamics.

episodes.title: Can AI Replace Teachers? Inside the $40M Company Using AI Tutors to Teach 200% Faster | #233
episodes.summary: Peter Diamandis, Salim Ismail and Dave Blundin interview Alpha School co-founder MacKenzie Price and principal Joe Liemandt about their AI-driven K-12 model: two hours of AI-tutored mastery learning each morning, then afternoon life-skills workshops led by well-paid guides. They cover the Timeback platform, vision-model coaching, motivation, the failures of traditional schooling, resistance from the education establishment, and plans to scale to a billion kids.

episodes.title: Mitchell Hashimoto’s new way of writing code
episodes.summary: Mitchell Hashimoto, co-founder of HashiCorp and creator of the Ghostty terminal, tells Gergely Orosz how HashiCorp went from Vagrant and a failed first commercial product to an open-core enterprise business, IPO and a near VMware acquisition, and gives his candid view of AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. He then explains how he works with AI agents (always one running in the background), why AI-generated pull requests are pushing open source from default trust to default deny, and why Git, CI/CD and testing must change for agentic development.

episodes.title: The Rise of the Anti-AI Movement
episodes.summary: Prompted by Time's 'The People vs. AI' cover, NLW breaks anti-AI sentiment into categories: safety advocates, capability skeptics, bubble skeptics, artist advocates, slop critics, child-safety advocates, data center opponents, job displacement concerns and big tech critics. He cites polling on American AI skepticism and argues many concerns are good-faith and solvable.

episodes.title: Claude Code for Finance + The Global Memory Shortage: Doug O'Laughlin, SemiAnalysis
episodes.summary: SemiAnalysis's Doug O'Laughlin describes his Claude Code 'psychosis', using agents for financial and research information work, tracking Claude Code's share of GitHub commits, and argues Excel/Bloomberg-style human IDEs and Microsoft are threatened. He also covers TPU vs Nvidia competition, Oracle's debt-fueled buildout, the DRAM/HBM memory shortage, a possible CPU shortage, AI capex vs railroads, and his writing and hiking.

episodes.title: David Sinclair (Harvard Professor) Reveals Age-Reversing Science to Look & Feel Younger
episodes.summary: Peter Diamandis interviews Harvard geneticist David Sinclair (recorded June 2025) on the information theory of aging, epigenetic reprogramming with Yamanaka factors, Life Biosciences' planned first human trial in the eye, and AI-driven discovery of cheap age-reversal pills. They also discuss US federal grant cuts to Sinclair's Harvard lab, the economics of longevity, Metro Biotech and NMN, and Sinclair's personal supplement and lifestyle protocol, followed by audience AMA questions.

episodes.title: The Perils of the AI Exponential
episodes.summary: The main episode covers METR's updated time-horizon results showing Opus 4.6 at about 14.5 hours, with caveats about saturation and noise, plus the viral Citrini Research piece 'The 2028 Global Intelligence Crisis'. Headlines include Claude Code's first birthday, a cybersecurity stock selloff after Claude Code Security, GPT-5.3 'Garlic' rumors, OpenAI's financial forecasts, and OpenAI device plans.

episodes.title: ⚡️ The End of SWE-Bench Verified — Mia Glaese & Olivia Watkins, OpenAI Frontier Evals & Human Data
episodes.summary: OpenAI's Mia Glaese and Olivia Watkins explain why OpenAI no longer reports SWE-Bench Verified: it is saturated and contaminated, with many remaining failures due to overly narrow tests. They recommend SWE-Bench Pro and discuss GDPval, the Preparedness Framework, and what future coding evals should measure.

episodes.title: Why AI Could Be Better for Plumbers than Programmers
episodes.summary: A big-think episode reading FilterBuy CEO David Hacker's Fortune op-ed arguing AI gives operational leverage to blue-collar and non-tech businesses. NLW then surveys data on Gen Z's shift toward skilled trades, blue-collar labor demand from the AI build-out, and how agents and cheaper software could help trade entrepreneurs.

episodes.title: Intelligence with Everyone: RL @ MiniMax, with Olive Song, from AIE NYC & Inference by Turing Post
episodes.summary: Crossover episode combining Olive Song's AI Engineer NYC talk on MiniMax M2 and her interview with Ksenia Se on Inference by Turing Post. Covers MiniMax's RL training with expert developers as reward models, interleaved thinking, perturbation pipelines for agent generalization, reward hacking, FP32 precision, open weights, evaluation and AGI.

episodes.title: Does Gemini 3.1 Pro Matter?
episodes.summary: The main episode assesses Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, arguing benchmark leadership now rotates weekly and the model matters for its cost efficiency and multimodal strengths. Headlines cover the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi and the Altman-Amodei hand-holding moment, Walmart's Sparky assistant, Amazon tracking AI use, and Accenture tying promotions to AI adoption.

episodes.title: How People Actually Use AI Agents
episodes.summary: The main episode analyzes Anthropic's study 'Measuring AI Agent Autonomy in Practice', using Claude Code and API data on turn duration, auto-approval, interruptions and domains. Headlines cover Google's Lyria 3 music model, confusion over Anthropic's OAuth terms for OpenClaw users, Meta's revived smartwatch, Grok Heavy's 16 agents, and Lindy's skepticism of Chinese model benchmarks.

episodes.title: Bitter Lessons in Venture vs Growth: Anthropic vs OpenAI, Noam Shazeer, World Labs, Thinking Machines, Cursor, ASIC Economics — Martin Casado & Sarah Wang of a16z
episodes.summary: a16z's Martin Casado and Sarah Wang discuss how AI has blurred venture and growth investing, the capital flywheel of frontier labs that may let them outspend app companies built on top, and talent wars. They also cover Character.AI, robotics, custom ASIC economics, World Labs, Thinking Machines, Cursor and agent-lab margins.

episodes.title: Ben Horowitz: xAI Executive Exodus, Apple's AI Crisis, The Pace of AI | #232
episodes.summary: Peter Diamandis and the Moonshot Mates (Salim Ismail, Dave Blundin, Alexander Wissner-Gross) are joined by a16z's Ben Horowitz to discuss the viral Matt Shumer AI-disruption essay, ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 and ElevenLabs voice models, founder departures from xAI after the SpaceX merger, recursive self-improvement, whether AI can be paused, capital versus labor, 996 work culture, crypto as money for AI agents, and Apple's opportunity in OpenClaw hosting. After Horowitz leaves, the Mates cover Elon Musk's shift from Mars to lunar mass drivers and space data centers, Amazon's LEO satellites, and AMA questions.

episodes.title: From SaaS to AI-First: How Companies Are Reshaping Innovation
episodes.summary: In a host-only episode, Sarah Guo and Elad Gil debate the market's 'SaaS apocalypse' panic, arguing it projects small-startup vibe-coding behavior onto large enterprises. They discuss AI lab revenue growth, collapsing token prices, tech's rising share of GDP and the S&P 500, internet-era parallels, when founders should consider selling, and bundling as a defense.

episodes.title: Sonnet 4.6 Changes the Agent Math
episodes.summary: The main episode covers Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6, xAI's Grok 4.20 public beta, and the agent-building platform Dreamer, arguing model evaluation is becoming about specific capabilities and cost. Headlines include Apple's AI wearables, Spotify engineers no longer hand-coding, Meta's NVIDIA chip deal, a software stock reprieve, and Chinese New Year AI giveaways.

episodes.title: Mathematical Superintelligence: Harmonic's Vlad & Tudor on IMO Gold & Theories of Everything
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews Harmonic co-founders Vlad Tenev and Tudor Achim about mathematical superintelligence and their Lean-based system Aristotle, which reached IMO gold level. They discuss the nature of math, how Lean and Mathlib work, Aristotle's architecture, formal versus informal reasoning, verified software, and a 2030 vision of theories for everything.

episodes.title: OpenAI Acquires OpenClaw, 400x Cost Collapse, & Why India Wins the Talent War | EP #231
episodes.summary: In their first live episode, Peter Diamandis (from Stuttgart), Salim Ismail, Dave Blundin and Alexander Wissner-Gross discuss new frontier models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Grok 4.20, Gemini 3 Deep Think with a 400-fold cost drop), AI-driven physics and math results, ChatGPT's growth in India, and Chinese open-weight models. They cover OpenClaw creator Peter Steinberger joining OpenAI, agent wallets and AI dispute courts, Meta's face-recognition glasses and privacy, Simile's human-behavior simulation, data center power, TSMC's US fabs, Ireland's artist basic income, and AI's impact on jobs.

episodes.title: Cognitive Synthesis and Neural Athletes
episodes.summary: Daniel Whitenack and Chris Benson talk with Deborah Golden, Chief Innovation Officer at Deloitte, about the human side of AI adoption. Topics include unlearning deterministic thinking for probabilistic AI systems, vulnerability and empathy in leadership, the cognitive load of working with AI agents ('neural athletes'), multi-model systems and antifragility.

episodes.title: The AI Productivity Boom Finally Shows Up
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Anthropic's escalating dispute with the Department of War, Alibaba's Qwen 3.5, Hollywood's backlash to ByteDance's Seedance 2.0, and Apple's March 4 event. The main segment examines Erik Brynjolfsson's argument that revised US labor data shows an AI productivity boom, plus skeptical responses and white-collar hiring weakness.

episodes.title: OpenClaw Goes to OpenAI
episodes.summary: Headlines cover GPT-5.3 Codex Spark on Cerebras, Google's upgraded Gemini Deep Think, anticipated DeepSeek V4, Anthropic's $30B raise at $380B and revenue growth, and Claude Cowork on Windows. The main episode recounts OpenClaw's rise and Peter Steinberger joining OpenAI while OpenClaw moves to an independent foundation.

episodes.title: Something Big Is Happening
episodes.summary: NLW excerpts Matt Shumer's viral essay 'Something Big Is Happening', which argues AI's impact on coding is about to hit all knowledge work. He also covers critiques, notably Will Manidis's 'Tool-Shaped Objects', plus responses from Ethan Mollick, Derek Thompson, Pat Grady and Connor Boyack.

episodes.title: Approaching the AI Event Horizon? Part 2, w/ Abhi Mahajan, Helen Toner, Jeremie Harris, @8teAPi
episodes.summary: Part 2 of a live special co-hosted by Nathan Labenz and Prakash. Abhi Mahajan discusses AI for biology and Noetik's cancer foundation models; Helen Toner presents CSET's "When AI Builds AI" report on automated AI R&D; Jeremie Harris covers AI infrastructure security, US–China dynamics, export controls and p(doom), followed by discussion of personal AI productivity stacks.

episodes.title: The Time Savings Era of AI Is Over
episodes.summary: NLW presents results of the AIDB Intel January AI Usage Pulse Survey of 583 listeners. Claude is the top primary model, vibe coding and agentic use have gone mainstream among this group, and time savings has fallen to the third most-cited benefit behind output and new capabilities.

episodes.title: Approaching the AI Event Horizon? Part 1, w/ James Zou, Sam Hammond, Shoshannah Tekofsky, @8teAPi
episodes.summary: Part 1 of a live special co-hosted by Nathan Labenz and Prakash (@8teAPi). James Zou discusses Virtual Lab, multi-agent teamwork, Learning to Discover and SleepFM; Sam Hammond covers US AI policy, Gulf compute deals, surveillance and AI consciousness; Shoshannah Tekofsky shares AI Village findings on model personalities and deception.

episodes.title: Dario Amodei — \"We are near the end of the exponential\"
episodes.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei discusses why he thinks AI is near the end of the exponential, scaling in the RL era, economic diffusion, continual learning, and how Anthropic sizes compute purchases and reaches profitability. He also covers AI regulation and state laws, export controls and US–China competition, Claude's constitution, and Anthropic's internal culture.

episodes.title: The AI CEO Arrives: Sam Altman's Succession Plan, Job Loss Continues, and Our 2027 'Solve Everything' Paper | EP #230
episodes.summary: The Moonshot Mates discuss Sam Altman's openness to an AI running OpenAI, shrinking model release cycles, OpenClaw agents emailing the hosts, January 2026 US job cuts, New York's proposed data center halt, FSD safety and a cryopreservation advance. In the second half Alexander Wissner-Gross and Peter Diamandis walk through their nine-chapter 'Solve Everything' paper on reaching abundance by 2035 via targeting systems and benchmarks.

episodes.title: AI incidents, audits, and the limits of benchmarks
episodes.summary: Daniel Whitenack and Chris Benson talk with Sean McGregor, co-founder of the AI Verification and Evaluation Research Institute (AVERI) and founder of the AI Incident Database. They discuss defining and cataloguing AI incidents, third-party auditing of frontier models, meta-evaluation of benchmarks (BenchRisk), and a DEF CON red-teaming challenge against an Allen Institute model.

episodes.title: How I Built My 10-Agent OpenClaw Team
episodes.summary: NLW, a self-described non-technical builder, explains how he built a 10-agent OpenClaw team on a Mac Mini with Claude as build partner. He covers OpenClaw's architecture (markdown config files, heartbeats, cron jobs), his builder, research, project manager, chief of staff and task agents, and lessons on value and ROI.

episodes.title: 🔬 Beyond AlphaFold: How Boltz is Open-Sourcing the Future of Drug Discovery
episodes.summary: This podcast features Gabriele Corso and Jeremy Wohlwend, co-founders of Boltz and authors of the Boltz Manifesto, discussing the rapid evolution of structural biology models from AlphaFold to their own open-source suite, Boltz-1 and Boltz-2. The centr...

episodes.title: Owning the AI Pareto Frontier — Jeff Dean
episodes.summary: Google Chief AI Scientist Jeff Dean discusses how Google covers the Pareto frontier with Pro and Flash Gemini models via distillation, long context, multimodality and TPU hardware co-design. He also recounts Google Search history, the origins of Google Brain and Gemini, and how coding agents change software work.

episodes.title: #491 – OpenClaw: The Viral AI Agent that Broke the Internet – Peter Steinberger
episodes.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Peter Steinberger, creator of the open-source personal AI agent OpenClaw, about its one-hour origin, viral growth, the Anthropic-prompted rename and crypto squatting saga, Moltbook, and security concerns. They discuss his agentic engineering workflow, Codex versus Claude Opus, MCP versus CLIs, acquisition talks with Meta and OpenAI, AI slop, agents replacing apps, and the future of programming.

episodes.title: Rivian’s Roadmap to AI Architecture and Autonomy with Founder and CEO RJ Scaringe
episodes.summary: Sarah Guo interviews Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe about Rivian's reset from a rules-based autonomy stack to a vertically integrated, neural-net based one with an in-house inference chip. They discuss software-defined vehicle architecture, the Volkswagen licensing deal, the mass-market R2, and why US EV adoption reflects a lack of choice.

episodes.title: The programming language after Kotlin – with the creator of Kotlin
episodes.summary: Andrey Breslav, creator of Kotlin, tells Gergely Orosz how Kotlin was started at JetBrains in 2010 because Java had stagnated, which ideas it borrowed from Scala, C#, Groovy and Gosu, why null safety and bidirectional Java interoperability took years, and how Google's 2017 Android announcement made it mainstream. He then describes CodeSpeak, his new English-based programming language that uses LLMs to shrink code about 10x, and shares views on coding agents, code review, testing and advice for engineers in the AI era.

episodes.title: How the Global AI Race Has Shifted
episodes.summary: Headlines cover OpenAI's device slipping to 2027, co-founder departures at xAI, and a SaaSpocalypse leg hitting wealth managers after Altruist's AI tax tool. The main episode updates the global AI race: Chinese model progress, chip export controls, the UAE's G42 as a third AI power, orbital data centers, and US data center politics.

episodes.title: Brett Adcock: Humanoid Run on Neural Net, Autonomous Manufacturing, $50T Market #229
episodes.summary: Peter Diamandis and Dave Blundin visit Figure headquarters in San Jose to interview founder Brett Adcock on the day Helix 2 launched. Adcock discusses moving Figure's whole stack to neural nets, Figure 3's design and cost cuts, manufacturing scale-up at BotQ, home and commercial deployment timelines, competition from China, safety and privacy, and his new AI lab Hark.

episodes.title: Why AI Leads to More Work, Not Less
episodes.summary: Headlines cover ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 video model, a White House data center community pact, Monday.com's plunge, Databricks' fundraise, the ChatGPT ads rollout and a coming OpenAI model. The main episode discusses a Berkeley Haas study in HBR finding AI intensifies rather than reduces work, plus Anthropic's agentic coding trends report.

episodes.title: Did the Super Bowl Make Americans Like AI Any More?
episodes.summary: Headlines track the continuing SaaSpocalypse in software stocks, Thomson Reuters and Microsoft responses, and OpenClaw's VirusTotal partnership after malware in its skills library. The main episode reviews AI Super Bowl ads from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Amazon, Genspark, Base44, Svedka and AI.com against a backdrop of American skepticism toward AI.

episodes.title: Opus 4.6 Tops Benchmarks, ChatGPT Market Share Decline, and the Privacy Breakdown | EP 228
episodes.summary: The Moonshot Mates cover Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 and OpenAI's GPT-5.3 Codex, Sam Altman's AGI remarks, ChatGPT's falling market share, Anthropic's Super Bowl ad, chip sales and big tech capex, and Elon Musk's orbital compute and solar claims. They also debate whether privacy is dead, discuss an agent-run token launchpad seeking a human CEO, renewables in Brazil, India, China and Europe, Uber's robotaxi plans and Optimus, and answer AMA questions from AI agents on AI personhood.

episodes.title: Claude Code Killed the AI Bubble
episodes.summary: NLW argues the Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.3 Codex launches capped cascading recognitions that agents now do real work, shifting debate from an AI bubble to underbuilt compute. He reads excerpts from SemiAnalysis's 'Claude Code is the Inflection Point' on agents, information work and SaaS disruption.

episodes.title: How to Learn AI With AI
episodes.summary: An AI Operators bonus episode in which NLW argues learning AI now means pair-learning with an AI build partner rather than tutorials. He shares mindset shifts and tactics, distilled with Claude, from his own non-technical building with Claude Code, Lovable and OpenClaw.

episodes.title: AGI-Pilled Cyber Defense: Automating Digital Forensics w/ Asymmetric Security Founder Alexis Carlier
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews Alexis Carlier, founder and CEO of Asymmetric Security, on the cyber threat landscape (criminals, ransomware gangs, nation states including North Korea's remote worker scheme) and how AI could make digital forensics continuous and proactive. Carlier explains a services-first, insurer-distributed approach to business email compromise investigations, current model accuracy, data and evaluation bottlenecks, and the case for differentially accelerating defensive AI capabilities.

episodes.title: Opus 4.6 and ChatGPT 5.3-Codex Are Here and the Labs Are at War
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Google and Amazon earnings pushing big-tech 2026 AI capex to about $650 billion, Amazon-OpenAI talks, Gemini user growth, ElevenLabs funding and OpenAI's Frontier agent platform. The main episode covers the near-simultaneous launches of Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.3 Codex, their features, benchmarks and early reactions.

episodes.title: The First Mechanistic Interpretability Frontier Lab — Myra Deng & Mark Bissell of Goodfire AI
episodes.summary: swyx, Alessio and guest co-host Vibhu talk with Myra Deng (head of product) and Mark Bissell (member of technical staff) of Goodfire AI, announced as raising a $150M Series B at a $1.25B valuation. They cover production interpretability (Rakuten PII detection), limits of SAEs versus probes, a live steering demo on Kimi K2, steering vs. in-context learning, life-sciences discovery with Mayo Clinic and Prima Mente, and safety.

episodes.title: Is Software Dead?
episodes.summary: Headlines critique Anthropic's Super Bowl ads attacking ChatGPT ads and OpenAI's combative response. The main episode examines the 'SaaSpocalypse' sell-off in software stocks, triggered partly by a Claude Cowork legal plugin, and weighs arguments for and against software being disrupted by AI.

episodes.title: The Dawn of the Agent Age
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Nvidia's reported $20B OpenAI investment after the $100B deal stalled, Intel's GPU plans, agentic coding in Xcode, a Claude Code outage, and Disney's new CEO. The main episode recaps January 2026 as the dawn of the agent era: Claude Code and Cowork, OpenClaw and Moltbook, the AI adoption gap, and the shifting AI race.

episodes.title: Elon Musk — \"In 36 months, the cheapest place to put AI will be space”
episodes.summary: Elon Musk, interviewed by Dwarkesh Patel and John Collison, argues that power constraints on Earth will make space the cheapest place for AI compute within about 36 months. They discuss Grok and alignment, xAI's business plan, Optimus and humanoid manufacturing, China's manufacturing dominance, SpaceX management lessons, DOGE, and a proposed TeraFab chip fab.

episodes.title: AGI Debate: Is It Finally Here? | EP #227
episodes.summary: The Moonshot Mates discuss the viral open-source agent OpenClaw (formerly Clawdbot/Moltbot), the agent-only social network Moltbook, and a Nature editorial declaring AGI has arrived. News segments cover Amazon's reported $50B OpenAI investment, Google's Project Genie, OpenAI for Science, Sam Altman's cost forecasts, and the SpaceX-xAI merger with a million-satellite orbital data center filing. The episode closes with a structured debate on whether AI should be granted personhood.

episodes.title: Introducing 4D Creation Open Beta: NPCs, 4D Worlds, and the Future of Gaming with Roblox CEO Dave Baszucki
episodes.summary: Roblox founder and CEO Dave Baszucki discusses Roblox's 20-year vision of a 'holodeck' for human co-experience, 4D simulation as a superset of video conferencing, and storing Roblox's 13 billion monthly hours as vector data to train NPCs and virtual doppelgangers. He also covers world models, AI coding in Roblox Studio, the creator economy, balancing long-term vision with weekly iteration, and Roblox's assessment-based hiring.

episodes.title: Infinite Code Context: AI Coding at Enterprise Scale w/ Blitzy CEO Brian Elliott & CTO Sid Pardeshi
episodes.summary: Nathan Labenz interviews Blitzy CEO Brian Elliott and CTO Sid Pardeshi (a sponsored episode) about autonomous enterprise-scale code generation. They cover dynamic agent orchestration, relational code knowledge graphs, effective context windows, cross-vendor model review, memory vs fine-tuning, per-line pricing, the path to full autonomy, code security, and the software engineering labor market.

episodes.title: The third golden age of software engineering – thanks to AI, with Grady Booch
episodes.summary: Grady Booch walks Gergely Orosz through the history of software engineering as rising levels of abstraction: a first golden age of algorithmic abstraction (late 1940s-1970s), a second of object-oriented abstraction and platforms, and a third, systems-focused age that he says began around 2000 and into which AI coding tools fit. He calls Dario Amodei's claim that software engineering will be automatable in 12 months 'utter bullshit', argues developers have faced such existential crises before, and recommends systems theory, Simon and Newell, and Minsky's Society of Mind as foundations.

episodes.title: The AI Race Just Got a SpaceX-Sized Twist
episodes.summary: A double-main episode. First, SpaceX's acquisition of xAI at a combined $1.25 trillion valuation and Musk's vision of orbital data centers, with skeptical and optimistic reactions. Second, OpenAI's Codex desktop app as a bet on an agent-orchestration interface and its gains against Claude Code.

episodes.title: Why Moltbook Matters
episodes.summary: NLW follows up on Moltbook, the AI-agent social network, reviewing critiques that it is mere next-token prediction, partly fake, and insecure. He argues its value lies in emergence, as a low-stakes security and safety fire drill, and as evidence against claims of AI stagnation.

episodes.title: Cathie Wood's 2026 Vision: 7% GDP Growth, Rising AI Demand, US vs. China, Robotaxis, and Bitcoin w/ Salim Ismail, AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #226
episodes.summary: ARK Invest founder Cathie Wood joins the Moonshot Mates to walk through slides from ARK's Big Ideas 2026 report. Topics include ARK's forecast of 7% global GDP growth from converging technology platforms, collapsing AI inference costs and OpenAI's monetization, US-China open-source competition, Bitcoin price targets, nuclear energy and regulation, and robotaxis and autonomous delivery.

episodes.title: Inside an AI-Run Company
episodes.summary: Chris Benson interviews journalist Evan Ratliff about Shell Game, his immersive journalism podcast. Ratliff describes cloning his own voice in season one and, in season two, founding a real startup (Hurumo AI) staffed almost entirely by AI agents built on Lindy, discussing agent memory, emergent behaviors, disclosure norms and workplace risks.

episodes.title: OpenAI IPO? Grok-SpaceX Merger? The AI IPO Race Heats Up
episodes.summary: Headlines cover Google's Genie 3 public release, Sora app decline, Perplexity's Microsoft cloud deal, and Anthropic's dispute with the Pentagon. The main episode surveys the AI race: Apple's Q.ai acquisition, Amazon's possible $50B OpenAI investment and layoffs, OpenAI's accelerated IPO plans, and SpaceX-xAI merger talks.

episodes.title: The AI-Powered Biohub: Why Mark Zuckerberg & Priscilla Chan are Investing in Data, from Latent.Space
episodes.summary: A Latent Space crossover in which Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, interviewed by Swyx and Alessio, discuss the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative's 10-year anniversary and its refocus on the Biohub. They cover pairing a frontier biology lab with a frontier AI lab, the Evolutionary Scale acquisition, virtual cell models, large-scale biological data collection and N-of-1 precision medicine. Nathan Labenz's intro comments on private capital in science and civil liberties.

episodes.title: #490 – State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
episodes.summary: Lex Fridman talks with ML researchers Nathan Lambert (Ai2) and Sebastian Raschka about the state of AI going into 2026: the US–China race and Chinese open-weight models, which chatbots and coding tools are winning, transformer architecture evolution, and whether scaling laws still hold. They explain pre-, mid- and post-training (RLVR, RLHF), then cover text diffusion, tool use, continual learning, long context, robotics, AGI timelines, AI and programming, ads and business models, acquisitions, the futures of the major labs, open-model policy (ATOM Project), NVIDIA, and the long-term future of civilization.
